title: Region of the star Sadr in the constellation Cygnus

html:
Here is an image of the region of the star Sadr, at the center of the image, in the constellation Cygnus. Sadr is located about 1300 light-years away and is 13 times more massive than our sun.

The Sadr region is occupied by a diffuse emission nebula (IC 1318). These are the red regions in the image. The red comes from hydrogen. In particular the Butterfly Nebula just to the left.

Just north of Sadr, about 1/4 of the way into the image, we can see the open cluster NGC 6910 (The Rocking Horse Cluster), made up of 66 stars and located 3.6 light-years away.



Technical details
Telescope: Takahashi SKY90 II with dedicated f 4.5 focal reducer (407mm focal length)
Sensor: Canon 40D unfiltered
Filter: IDAS-LPS (to counter light pollution)
Mount: LX200 10" f 6.3 classic
Guiding: QHY5 ( KWIQ Guider) and PHD

40 frames of 300 seconds, 40 darks, 20 flats
Stacking in DeepSkyStacker
Processing in photoshop
